blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Claim verification is the task of deciding whether a source text supports a claim, contradicts it, or lacks sufficient evidence. Natural Language Inference (NLI) models can judge whether a single sentence supports or contradicts a claim, but they struggle when the evidence is spread across several sentences. Conversely, Large Language Models (LLMs) can reason across sentences, but may draw conclusions the text does not support. In this experimental study, we test whether a conservative fusion rule, labeling a claim Support or Contradict only when both models agree and defaulting to Not Enough Evidence otherwise, combines their strengths. We construct a benchmark of 2,035 claims from SciFact and CliniFact (858 Support, 152 Contradict, 1,025 Not Enough Evidence). We retrieve the top five most relevant sentences per claim using a hybrid of semantic and lexical (BM25) retrieval, which slightly outperforms either method alone. These retrieved sentences are then provided to every verification model. We then compare a DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli NLI baseline against Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 8B, and Mistral 7B. Qwen3 achieves the highest Macro-F1 (0.7937), followed by Llama 3.1 (0.7204) and Mistral (0.6388), while the NLI baseline reaches only 0.3157. Contrary to our hypothesis, fusion degrades performance, dropping Macro-F1 to 0.7392, 0.6730, and 0.5991, respectively. To understand this decline, we analyze agreements, disagreements, and common error patterns between the NLI and LLM verifiers. Our error analysis shows that NLI and LLM disagreements often result in correct LLM predictions being overturned.
blocks.zh: 索赔核实是决定来源文本是否支持索赔、是否与之相矛盾或是否缺乏充分证据的任务。 Natural Language Information(NLI)模型可以判断一个句子是支持还是与一个说法相矛盾,但是当证据分散在几个句子中时它们会挣扎. 反之,大语言模型(LLMS)可以跨句而行地解释,但可能会得出文本不支持的结论. 在这项实验性研究中,我们测试一个保守的聚变规则,在两种模型都同意和默认不足够证据的情况下,才标出索赔支持或矛盾,这是否结合了它们的优点。 我们从Scifact和CliniFact(858项支助,152项矛盾,1,025项证据不足)中确定了2 035项索赔的基准。 我们利用语义学和词汇学(BM25)的混合检索方法,检索每个索赔中最相关的前5个句子,这略高于任何一种方法。 然后将这些检索到的句子提供给每个核查模型。 然后,我们将DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli NLI基线与Llama 3.1 8B、Qune3 8B和Mistral 7B相比较。 Qune3实现了最高的Macro-F1 (0.7937),其次是Llama 3.1 (0.7204)和Mistral (0.6388),而NLI基线仅达到0.3157. 与我们的假设相反,聚变降解了性能,将Macro-F1分别降至0.7392,0.6730和0.5991. 为了理解这种下降,我们分析了NLI和LLM核查者之间的协议,分歧,以及常见的错误模式. 我们的错误分析表明,NLI和LLM的分歧往往导致正确的LLM预测被推翻.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The rapid growth of scientific literature has made it increasingly difficult to manually verify the claims presented in research publications, particularly as individual claims may be supported or contradicted by evidence distributed across multiple sections of a paper. Scientific
claim verification is the process of evaluating whether a specific
statement or hypothesis made in scientific literature is supported or
contradicted by underlying evidence [ 15 ] . This
process requires a strict protocol, mainly in the retrieval of text and
in the reasoning done using this evidence.

与基本证据相矛盾 [15]. 这个

在使用这些证据的推理中。

blocks.en:
Current verification systems rely on retrieval methods, natural language
inference (NLI) and LLMs. NLI models provide a constrained signal for
determining whether a claim is supported or contradicted by
evidence [ 9 ] , but may struggle when the required evidence
is distributed across multiple parts [ 21 ] . LLMs can
jointly reason over multiple pieces of retrieved context, but may produce
unsupported conclusions [ 6 ] . These complementary
characteristics motivate combining their predictions through a
conservative fusion strategy, where a claim is assigned “Support” or
“Contradict” only when both models agree. If not, the system abstains by
assigning “Not Enough Evidence”. We hypothesize that this agreement-based
strategy can reduce mistaken verdicts by requiring independent agreement
between the two approaches.

blocks.en: This study makes three contributions. First, we establish a common evaluation framework to compare a pretrained DeBERTa NLI model with three open-source LLMs: Qwen3 [ 20 ] , Llama [ 4 ] , and Mistral [ 7 ] , using a shared hybrid retrieval pipeline on a benchmark of 2,035 claims labeled as Support”, Contradict”, or Not Enough Evidence”. Second, we evaluate three NLI evidence aggregation strategies and investigate a conservative agreement-based fusion strategy that returns Support” or Contradict” only when the NLI model and LLM agree, assigning “Not Enough Evidence” otherwise. Third, we conduct a comparative evaluation and detailed error analysis to assess the effectiveness and limitations of these approaches. Our results show that standalone LLMs outperform the NLI model, and that the agreement-based fusion does not improve Macro-F1 over standalone LLMs. The error analysis further examines the factors contributing to this outcome.

blocks.en: 2.1 Scientific Claim Verification Datasets
blocks.zh: 2.1 科学索赔核实数据集

blocks.en:
The task of scientific claim verification was introduced as determining
whether a scientific claim is supported or contradicted by the evidence
given in the literature. Wadden et al. [ 15 ] introduced the
SciFact dataset, consisting of literature from actual research, with
scientific claims paired with abstracts containing the evidence, along with
labels and the rationales supporting each verification decision. This work
established a benchmark for systems that retrieve relevant evidence and
reason over it, rather than relying on prior scientific knowledge.

blocks.en: 2.2 Evidence Retrieval
blocks.zh: 2.2 取证

blocks.en:
Retrieving relevant evidence is the first step of a claim verification
pipeline. Lexical retrieval methods such as BM25 [ 14 ] rank documents by their term overlap with the claim and remain a strong
baseline across domains. Semantic or dense retrieval
methods encode the claim and the documents into a shared vector
space, allowing relevant evidence to be found even when it is worded
differently from the claim [ 8 ] .
However, dense retrievers trained on general-domain data can generalize
poorly to specialized domains such as scientific text. Hybrid retrieval fuses lexical and dense scores, for example through the combination of the two scores or reciprocal rank fusion, on the
belief that these two capture complementary notions of
relevance [ 2 ] , and such combinations can improve over
standalone method alone. For scientific
claim verification specifically, Wang et al. [ 17 ] used LLMs to
retrieve both corroborating and refuting evidence for a claim, highlighting
the importance of retrieving evidence on both sides of a claim.

blocks.en: 2.3 NLI-based Verification
blocks.zh: 2.3 以NLI为基础的核查

blocks.en:
Natural Language Inference (NLI) determines the relation between a given
statement and a text given as evidence. It generally indicates whether the
evidence supports or contradicts the statement, or whether there is not
enough information to determine the relation. This allows NLI to closely
mirror the steps involved in scientific claim verification, where a claim
needs to be evaluated against evidence from research literature.

声明和作为证据的文本。 它一般指出:
证据支持或与陈述相矛盾,或者不存在
足够信息来确定关系。 这样可以让 NLI 接近
反映科学索赔核实中涉及的步骤,其中一项索赔
需要根据研究文献的证据进行评估。

blocks.en:
Košprdić et al. [ 9 ] used NLI for the task of scientific claim
verification. Their verification method includes a model fine-tuned on a
processed version of the SciFact dataset to determine whether a claim is
supported, contradicted, or lacks enough evidence. The authors fine-tune
multiple models, including RoBERTa Large, XLM-RoBERTa Large, DeBERTa, and
DeBERTa SQuAD, with the fine-tuned DeBERTa model achieving the highest weighted F1
score of 88% on a held-out split of their processed SciFact data. Their verification engine is part of a larger scientific
question answering system, where documents retrieved from PubMed are used
as evidence for verification. However, NLI models are typically trained on
sentence-level pairs, and their performance degrades when evidence spans
multiple sentences or an entire document [ 21 ] .
They have also been shown to rely on shallow heuristics that do not
generalize beyond their training data.

blocks.en: 2.4 LLM-based Claim Verification
blocks.zh: 2.4 基于LLM的索赔核实

blocks.en:
The development of LLMs has opened a new avenue of approach to the task of
scientific claim verification, as these models can process a claim together
with the evidence text and generate the required verification decision.
Existing works have used LLMs for zero-shot and evidence-grounded
verification, including methods that take citation texts or retrieved text
as part of the input [ 1 ] . These studies
use LLMs to perform claim verification reasoning without the need for a
task-specific classifier for every verification setting. However,
differences in prompting, model size, evidence selection and output
analysis make direct comparison between these LLMs
difficult [ 3 ] . This motivates comparing multiple
open-source LLMs under the same retrieval and evaluation conditions.

blocks.en: 4 Methodology
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en: 4.1 System Overview
blocks.zh: 4.1 系统概况

blocks.en:
Given a claim and a source text, our experimental framework determines
whether the claim is “Support”, “Contradict”, or “Not Enough
Evidence” according to the source text. As shown in
Figure 1 , the framework is a multi-stage pipeline:
sentence retrieval, NLI-based verification, LLM-based verification, and
an optional fusion step that combines the NLI and LLM verdicts.

图1 框架是一个多阶段管道:
句子检索、基于 NLI 的核查、基于 LLM 的核查,以及

blocks.en:
For each of the 2,035 claims, the top five most relevant sentences for
each claim–source pair are retrieved using a hybrid retrieval
configuration (Section 4.2 ). Subsequently, the
retrieved sentences and their relevance scores are stored in a
retrieval cache. All later steps read the top five sentences from this
cache, so every model operates on exactly the same retrieved data and
differences in performance come from the models, not from retrieval.

blocks.en: 4.6 Conservative Hybrid Fusion
blocks.zh: 4.6 保守混合组合

blocks.en:
To combine the NLI and LLM verification outputs, we employ a conservative
agreement-based fusion strategy. The verdicts produced by the NLI and LLM
verifiers are reused directly in the fusion step, without performing an
additional LLM inference. If the NLI and LLM predictions
agree, their shared verdict is returned; otherwise, the claim is classified
as “Not Enough Evidence”. This strategy prioritizes precision and
avoids accepting a claim when the two independent verification methods
disagree.

基于协议的核聚变战略。 NLI和LLM作出的判决
核查器在核聚变步骤中直接重复使用,不执行
额外的LLM推论. 如果NLI和LLM预测

避免在两种独立核查方法时接受索赔要求
意见不一。

blocks.en: 5.1 Models and Implementation
blocks.zh: 5.1 模式和实施

blocks.en:
The verification pipeline uses DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli as the NLI
baseline and three open-source large language models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 8B,
and Mistral 7B. All LLMs are evaluated under the same prompt and evidence
conditions with a temperature of 0, and no model is fine-tuned on the evaluation
data. The LLMs are run locally on an RTX 4080 mobile GPU using Ollama with
quantized model variants. Qwen3 is evaluated with its thinking mode disabled
to maintain a consistent direct-verdict setting across models. Each LLM
response is parsed as JSON to extract the final verdict.

evaluation. We evaluate the standalone NLI and LLM verifiers as well as
the corresponding NLI–LLM fusion systems.

blocks.en: 8 Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 8 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
The benchmark is dominated by CliniFact, which contributes 1,587
claims compared with 448 SciFact claims. In addition,
“Contradict” claims come only from SciFact, while “Not Enough Evidence”
claims come only from CliniFact. Thus, some of the observed performance
differences maybe due to the differences between the two datasets.
Future work can evaluate the approach on benchmarks with a more balanced
distribution of both datasets and labels. Our experiments also use
zero-shot NLI and compact LLMs with fixed inference settings.
Testing fine-tuned models, additional LLMs, and different model sizes
would provide a broader comparison. Finally, the fusion method uses a
simple agreement rule and treats both verifiers equally. More
sophisticated fusion methods could account for the confidence of each
prediction and the reliability of each verifier.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en:
We investigated whether combining NLI with LLM-based verification using a conservative fusion rule can improve claim verification. To provide a strong and consistent evidence set to our verifiers we used a hybrid retrieval approach, that
outperformed both semantic-only and BM25-only retrieval in terms of
MRR and mean Recall. We also evaluated three NLI evidence aggregation
strategies and found that relevance-weighted aggregation performed
best on the development set. On the final benchmark, Qwen3 8B achieved
the strongest standalone performance (Macro-F1 0.7937), substantially
outperforming the NLI baseline (0.3157). Although NLI and
LLMs made different errors, our conservative agreement-based fusion did
not effectively combine their strengths and reduced Macro-F1 for all
three LLMs. These results show that stronger retrieval and diverse
verifiers alone are not sufficient for effective fusion, future
approaches should account for verifier confidence and reliability when
resolving disagreements.
